accent.note: The operator color. Theme-dependent; Ocean and Amber are deepened so their foreground clears contrast.

accent-hover.note: Darkens in light themes, brightens in dark ones — the inversion keeps hover legible on a dark ground.

accent-subtle.note: Selection and local-user tint; the accent at panel weight.

on-accent.note: Foreground for accent fills. White in light themes, a near-black from the accent hue in dark ones.

bg-base.note: Page ground; also the recessed fill for inputs on a surface.

bg-surface.note: Cards, panels, headers, modals, the roster panel.

bg-muted.note: The recessed tone: control tray, meter well, disabled fills, badge fills.

text-secondary.note: Section and field labels, inactive control glyphs.

text-muted.note: Placeholders, hints, counts. Clears 4.5:1 on both grounds in every theme.

border.note: The hairline doing nearly all separation work. Clears 3:1 in every theme.

success-500.note: A mic is open, a peer is present, the connection is live.

error-500.note: Muted, deafened, at capacity, disconnected, destructive.

display.purpose: The join screen title. Once per screen at most.

headline.purpose: Modal titles and the room title.

title.purpose: Participant names, keycap badge, form inputs.

body.purpose: Chat messages, empty-state copy, modal subtitles.

caption.purpose: Section headers and field labels. Uppercase, 700, 0.05em — the workhorse.

micro.purpose: Nav items, mode labels, counts. Tracking widens as size shrinks.

readout.purpose: Live numeric values only; monospace stops digits jittering.

scaleDebt.note: The frontmatter records what the code contains, not an intended scale. These clusters are drift and should collapse.

shadows.name: shadow-sm
shadows.purpose: Seated: cards at rest, headers, control buttons, keycap badge.

shadows.name: shadow-md
shadows.purpose: Lifted: hover, mobile PTT button, reconnect banner.

shadows.name: shadow-lg
shadows.purpose: Floating: modals, sheets, popovers, join card.

shadows.name: glow-brand
shadows.purpose: Accent glow under the brand mark only.

shadows.name: glow-primary
shadows.purpose: Accent glow under the primary button.

shadows.name: glow-transmitting
shadows.purpose: Green glow under the mobile PTT button while transmitting.

shadows.name: ring-selected
shadows.purpose: Selection ring on the active theme chip.

motion.name: t-interactive
motion.value: background-color 0.2s ease, border-color 0.2s ease, color 0.2s ease, box-shadow 0.2s ease, transform 0.2s ease, opacity 0.2s ease
motion.purpose: Default state transition. Names its properties; `transition: all` is banned.

motion.name: t-interactive-fast
motion.purpose: Small targets react faster: tabs, chips, nav items.

motion.name: t-press
motion.purpose: Press feedback; fast enough to feel like the control answered the finger.

motion.name: ease-emphasized
motion.purpose: The mobile PTT button state change.

motion.name: press-scale
motion.purpose: Standard press feedback on every pressable surface.

breakpoints.name: grid
breakpoints.purpose: Room list becomes an auto-fill grid.

breakpoints.name: comfortable
breakpoints.purpose: Lobby padding, card radius, modal centers.

breakpoints.name: mobile
breakpoints.purpose: Chat panel loses its border; shell switches.

breakpoints.name: popover
breakpoints.purpose: Participant popover flips below its trigger.

layoutConstants.name: roster-panel
layoutConstants.purpose: Presence is glanced at; the panel stops growing once a card is comfortable.

layoutConstants.name: chat-measure
layoutConstants.purpose: Shared reading column for the message list and the composer.

layoutConstants.name: bubble-max
layoutConstants.purpose: Keeps line length readable in a wide chat area.

layoutConstants.name: touch-target
layoutConstants.purpose: Minimum hit area; carried on ::after where the drawn control is smaller.

themes.note: The identity is the thirteen-token structure; these eight sets are the worlds it renders in. scripts/check-contrast.mjs verifies 120 pairs across all of them and fails the build on a violation.

avatarPalette.note: The one sanctioned raw-hex set. A name is hashed to a stable index so a person is the same color for everyone, in every theme. Every swatch clears 4.5:1 with white initials, and no green or red hue appears — those carry state.

performanceMode.purpose: Applied when the tab is hidden. Force-disables every animation, transition, caret, backdrop-filter and glow.
performanceMode.constraint: Any motion, blur or glow must survive being switched off by this class; state must be readable from color, glyph and border alone.
performanceMode.note: Keyed to document.hidden on purpose — a window visible on a second monitor is being watched.

accessibility.contrastGate: npm run check:contrast — 120 pairs across 8 themes plus the avatar palette; exits non-zero on failure.
accessibility.focus: One global :focus-visible rule from the palette; no bare `outline: none` anywhere.
accessibility.dialogs: Every overlay carries role="dialog", aria-modal, a label, a focus trap and Escape.
accessibility.liveRegions: The chat message list is role="log" with aria-live="polite".
knownGaps: viewport meta sets user-scalable=0, blocking pinch zoom (WCAG 1.4.4)

narrative.overview:
VoiceRoom is a panel you glance at, not a page you read. Its users keep it open for hours in a background tab while doing something else; the interface’s whole job is to answer who is here, who is talking, can they hear me in the width of one look. So the system is built on restraint that isn’t timidity: the layout holds still, the type stays small and dense, and color is spent almost entirely on reporting state rather than on decorating surfaces.

The identity does not live in a palette, because there isn’t one fixed palette. Thirteen semantic tokens are redefined wholesale by eight named themes, and every component color routes through those thirteen names. What stays constant across all eight worlds is the structure: the spacing rhythm, the radius ladder, the weight hierarchy, and the roles the colors play. That invariance is the design system. Hue is the user’s; grammar is ours.

The component feel is tactile and physical. Voice controls are 48px squares seated in a recessed tray. The push-to-talk key renders as an actual keycap with a thickened 3px bottom border. Every pressable surface scales down on :active, and mobile controls fire a 15ms haptic tick.
keyCharacteristics: Thirteen semantic tokens, eight themes, no raw hex in component code.
Color reports state; it does not decorate. Green means a mic is open.
Emphasis at small sizes comes from weight and tracking, never from size.
Flat surfaces separated by hairline borders; shadow means floating or hovered.
Every state readable with all motion switched off.
Presence is glanced at, not studied: the roster is a panel, not the stage.

rules.name: The Thirteen Tokens Rule
rules.body: No component may contain a raw color value. The only sanctioned exceptions are the avatar identity palette, the five scrims, and the screen-share overlay’s close button, which draws on its own near-black ground regardless of theme.

rules.name: The Status Colors Adapt, Their Roles Do Not
rules.body: Success and error are redefined per theme. This supersedes an earlier rule that fixed them to single values: a single color cannot clear 4.5:1 against both a white and a near-black surface — the constraints are arithmetically incompatible. What stays constant is the meaning.

rules.name: The Tint, Don’t Pick Rule
rules.body: Status backgrounds and borders are derived via color-mix, at 8-15% for fills and 25-35% for borders. Never hand-pick a tint hex; it will only be right on one background.

rules.name: The One Loud Color Rule
rules.body: A single screen shows at most one accent-filled element competing for attention at rest.

rules.name: The Gate Runs
rules.body: npm run check:contrast verifies 120 token pairs across all eight themes plus the avatar palette. A ninth theme cannot ship with an unreadable pair. It exits non-zero.

rules.name: The Shout in Small Rule
rules.body: Emphasis at small sizes comes from weight, case, and letter-spacing — never from size.

rules.name: The Tracking Inversion Rule
rules.body: Tracking runs opposite to size. Above 1rem tighten; below 0.75rem open up.

rules.name: The Ellipsis Always Rule
rules.body: Every user-supplied string is nowrap + overflow hidden + ellipsis inside a min-width: 0 flex child. Names are capped at 20 characters on input, but nothing in the layout may grow to fit one.

rules.name: The Measure Rule
rules.body: Chat caps at --chat-measure (1040px) with bubbles at min(72%, 620px). The composer reads the same token, so the field lines up with the messages above it.

rules.name: The Ten Slot Rule
rules.body: The roster is capped at 10 participants server-side. Do not virtualize, do not paginate, do not design an overflow affordance — and one column is enough.

rules.name: The Two Shells Rule
rules.body: Desktop and mobile are separate components by design. A change that appears only in desktop-layout is half-shipped.

rules.name: The Shadow Means Airborne Rule
rules.body: A shadow appears when an element is literally above the page or responding to the pointer. A surface that is merely important gets a border and a tone.

rules.name: The Radius Ladder Rule
rules.body: Radius is a function of the element’s size and role. A new component picks a rung; it does not invent a value.

rules.name: The Chat Bubble Tail Rule
rules.body: Bubbles keep 12px on three corners and collapse to 2px on the corner nearest their sender. The only asymmetric radius in the system, and what makes authorship readable without an avatar.

rules.name: The Mute Wins Rule
rules.body: When a participant is both muted and producing audio, the mute indicator shows and the speaking ring is suppressed. State that constrains outranks state that merely reports.

rules.name: The Disabled Says Why Rule
rules.body: Every disabled control carries a reason in both title and aria-label — title alone never renders on touch.

rules.name: The Recessed Input Rule
rules.body: Inputs and trays sit one tone below their container. Nothing interactive floats above its parent’s tone.

rules.name: The Hover Capability Rule
rules.body: Every :hover rule is wrapped in @media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine). Touch devices synthesise hover on tap, and an ungated hover latches after a finger press. Where hover carries real feedback, the touch path gets it through :active.

rules.name: The Background Tab Rule
rules.body: app-background is applied when the tab is hidden and force-disables every animation, transition, caret, backdrop-filter and glow. Any motion you add must survive it, and the UI must remain legible without it. Keyed to document.hidden on purpose — a window visible on a second monitor is being watched.

rules.name: The Reduced Motion Rule
rules.body: prefers-reduced-motion collapses durations and stops looping animation, and drops movement outright on the speaking ring and status dots. Reduced motion means less movement, not a dead interface.

dos: Do route every color through the thirteen semantic tokens, and run npm run check:contrast before shipping a theme change.
Do use color-mix for status tints, at 8-15% for fills and 25-35% for borders.
Do reach for weight, uppercase and 0.05em tracking when something small needs emphasis, and leave the size alone.
Do give every user-supplied string min-width: 0 + nowrap + ellipsis, and every input a length bound.
Do pair every disabled state with a reason in both title and aria-label.
Do give every overlay role="dialog", a label, a focus trap and Escape.
Do draw controls at a comfortable size and carry the 44px target on a pseudo-element when the drawn size would be too heavy.
Do wrap every hover rule in @media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine).
Do put new room features in both shells.
donts: Don’t write a raw hex value in a component. The avatar palette, the five scrims and the pinned overlay close button are the only exceptions.
Don’t borrow a status color for anything that is not a state report, and don’t put a green or red hue in the avatar palette.
Don’t place more than one accent-filled element on a screen at rest.
Don’t add a shadow to convey importance.
Don’t invent a radius or a type size — and prefer the intended rungs over the drifted values this file records.
Don’t rely on animation to communicate a state.
Don’t design an overflow affordance for the participant list.
